claim_traces.claim_text: "Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short — around 5 feet 2 inches tall."
reasoning_steps: The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short is a well-documented historical myth
Following his death in 1821, his autopsy recorded his height as 5 pieds 2 pouces in pre-metric French units
A French inch (pouce) was longer than an English inch (approximately 2.7 cm compared to 2.54 cm)
When converted to modern imperial units, Napoleon was actually around 5 feet 6 inches to 5 feet 7 inches (approximately 1.68 to 1.69 meters) tall
This made him of average or slightly above average height for a French male in the early 19th century

The misconception of his shortness was perpetuated by the literal translation of the French measurements into English feet and inches, as well as contemporary British political propaganda (notably caricatures by James Gillray).

claim_traces.claim_title: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood
claim_traces.claim_text: "Octopuses have three hearts and their blood is blue."
reasoning_steps: Octopuses possess three hearts: two branchial hearts that pump deoxygenated blood through the gills to collect oxygen, and one systemic heart that pumps the oxygenated blood throughout the rest of the body

Furthermore, their blood is blue because it uses the copper-based protein hemocyanin rather than the iron-based hemoglobin found in vertebrates to transport oxygen, which appears blue when oxygenated and is adapted for cold, low-oxygen marine environments.
